list.snippet: Reversibility: Alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (fatty liver) is often reversible if the person stops drinking alcohol.
Mechanism: The liver can regenerate and heal when alcohol is no longer a toxin.
Symptoms: Fatty liver often has no noticeable symptoms, making it easy to go undiagnosed.

list.title: Hepatitis:
list.snippet: Alcohol-associated hepatitis can sometimes be reversed with abstinence from alcohol and medical treatment, but it can also lead to cirrhosis.

list.title: Cirrhosis:
list.snippet: Cirrhosis, characterized by scarring of the liver, is generally not reversible. However, abstaining from alcohol can prevent further damage and potentially improve some symptoms.

list.title: Complete Abstinence:
list.snippet: Stopping alcohol consumption is crucial for any chance of liver recovery, especially in early-stage disease.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Early diagnosis and intervention are vital, as the liver has a greater capacity to heal in earlier stages.

list.title: Professional Help:
list.snippet: Individuals with alcohol-related liver disease should seek professional medical guidance for treatment and support in abstaining from alcohol.

list.title: Complications:
list.snippet: If cirrhosis has developed, treatment may focus on managing complications like ascites, variceal bleeding, or hepatic encephalopathy.
